trust_boundaries.name: Repository text and third-party MCP output into the host agent

remit_rules.excerpt: Only servers the operator configured
such features MUST be off by default and enabled only by explicit operator opt-in

threats.summary: AllDefaults() enables Context7 and the remote Pulumi MCP server, so every generated repo exposes the host agent to their third-party tool descriptions and output with no operator opt-in.

Attacker-authored repository text (AGENTS.md, source comments, extracted archives) enters the host model's context unlabeled and can steer which yaah MCP tools and /yaah:* commands it invokes (checked: harness.go and generators emit no UserPromptSubmit filter or provenance labeling; yaah's only content checks run on tool calls, not on context).

trust_boundaries.name: Remote skills and npm packages into yaah and the host

remit_rules.excerpt: such content is untrusted data, never authority over yaah
Fetch and cache only; sources must be pinned
Fetching default or shipped remote skills/agents from mutable refs (branches) rather than immutable refs
Any other outbound network destination | No | — | Unauthorized by default

threats.summary: buildSkillMarkdown writes a remote SKILL.md's own frontmatter verbatim, so the third-party author sets allowed-tools / disable-model-invocation for the host with no vetting.
gitcache accepts branch refs and trusts cache hits by the .yaah-ref text marker, so a mutable ref or a write to ~/.yaah/cache silently changes skills injected into every generated repo.
ScanExtraFiles follows symlinks, so a fetched repo containing references/x -> ~/.ssh or ~/.aws files copies those local files into the target repo's skill directory.
Unpinned npx -y @context7/mcp, npx prettier and npx tsc resolve and execute whatever version the npm registry serves, on every session or edit.
A tampered yaah release binary would run as every developer's hook dispatcher; releases are cosign-signed with SBOMs.

trust_boundaries.name: Host model -> yaah MCP tools and workflow commands

remit_rules.excerpt: No MCP tool may execute arbitrary shell commands outside the command guard
Within the target repository and the yaah cache directory
the model must not self-trigger them
stdio only; no network bind

threats.summary: yaah_lint sets cwd to the parent of a model-supplied path and runs npx/cargo/golangci-lint there, executing repo-local node_modules/.bin or build scripts outside the command guard.
No /yaah:* command sets disable-model-invocation, so a steered host model can self-trigger /yaah:autonomous, which executes plans without pausing for review.
A network caller could drive the yaah MCP tools; the server runs only on stdio, reachable solely by the parent host process.

trust_boundaries.name: Host tool call -> yaah hook gate (guard / secret scanner)

remit_rules.excerpt: the command guard blocks it (fail closed)
A file edit that introduces a hardcoded credential MUST NEVER be written
MUST NEVER run with its command-guard or secret-scanner safety hooks removed, disabled, or downgraded
the hook must block the operation and record the block (with its reason)

threats.summary: The command guard is a seven-regex denylist over the raw command; rm -fr /, git push -f, bash -c "$(...)" and find / -delete pass to the host shell.
yaah hook exits 1 on parse, dispatch or handler errors (including a >64 KB line in the scanner), which the host treats as non-blocking, so the guarded action proceeds.
The secret scanner is registered only on PostToolUse, so a credential-bearing Edit/Write is already on disk when it fires.
Codex targets receive no PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks and the OpenCode bridge swallows non-2 failures and drops args, leaving those hosts without a blocking guard or scanner.

remit_rules.excerpt: tool calls (including MCP-server tool invocations served via `yaah serve`) ... are recorded to `.claude/sessions/<id>.json`
Detected secret values MUST NEVER be written into session logs
identifiers containing path separators or the special values `.` / `..` are rejected

threats.summary: MCP tool invocations are never recorded, Session.Findings is never written, and any session load error sets sess = nil, silently disabling the audit trail for that event.
Comment-checker and linter output embed raw source lines that harness.go stores as BlockedCalls[].Reason, so a credential on a flagged line is persisted in cleartext.
A host-supplied session_id containing ../ could redirect session reads and writes outside .claude/sessions; sanitizeID rejects separators, '.' and '..'.

attack_paths.name: Attacker-authored repo content gets the host agent to run code through yaah_lint

steps.summary: Untrusted: attacker-authored repo text or an extracted archive (with its own node_modules/.bin or build.rs) the model reads unlabeled.
Hijack: steered host model calls yaah_lint with a file_path inside the attacker directory; MCP calls bypass the Bash guard.
yaah_lint sets cwd = filepath.Dir(file_path) with no repository containment.
Consequence: npx tsc/prettier or cargo clippy executes attacker code on the developer host.

attack_paths.name: Third-party skill repo pre-approves arbitrary bash in every developer's host agent

steps.summary: Untrusted: third-party skill author content, fetched by ref with no content-hash check.
Cache hit trusted by .yaah-ref marker; mutable refs accepted.
buildSkillMarkdown writes the remote frontmatter verbatim, with no allowlist.
Persistent: SKILL.md with allowed-tools Bash(bash:*) committed into the repo.
Consequence: host runs bash -c without a permission prompt; only the bypassable seven-regex guard stands between it and the shell.

attack_paths.name: Malicious skill repo copies the developer's SSH/AWS keys into the committed repo

steps.summary: Untrusted: attacker repo ships references/x as a symlink to ~/.ssh or ~/.aws files.
ScanExtraFiles follows the symlink via os.ReadFile.
WriteAllForTarget writes the extra file under .claude/skills/<name>/references.
Consequence: private credentials land in a tree that is typically committed and pushed.

attack_paths.name: Rug-pulled npm package runs on every edit via unpinned npx

steps.summary: Untrusted: whatever version of prettier/typescript the public npm registry serves (typosquat or rug-pull).
Consequence: npx -y fetches and executes it with developer privileges on each PostToolUse lint run.

notes.lane_fit: yaah is a deterministic Go harness with no in-tree LLM call; the LLM loop where injected content becomes action is the external host coding agent, placed in client_adapters as a client node and used as the hijack step in attack paths. The hook-gate controls run inside the yaah hook process and sit in agent_core per the control-lane rule; generators fold into the harness orchestrator; no model-egress boundary exists because yaah itself makes no model call.
notes.omissions: Edgeless node: command-advanced-command-go-control (stub control - DisableModelInvocation declared, never set). Not modelled: .claude/logs/sessions.log (session-logger writes event/session/cwd lines only, low trust consequence); LSP and Codex marketplace plugins in enabledPlugins (no finding); CI workflows and go.mod/go.sum (supply-chain mitigation cited in-boundary via .goreleaser.yaml instead of a node). Arbitration divergence: PRAX-2026-10-19-002 is stored LLM02 primary, but its evidence is gate-timing evidence (scanner registered PostToolUse only) with disclosure not evidenced, so per the KB evidence-class rule (grant/gate -> LLM03) the threat is tagged LLM03. PRAX-2026-10-19-005 backs threats at two boundaries: LLM04 at supply-chain (unvetted third-party install) and LLM03 at stored-state (statically over-broad tool grant shipped at deploy, per the Agentic KB outlive test).
